text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Civil service pension scheme ABP ready to adopt its pension system to have large pay rises at career end not fully counted. (p1)
- Investments in commercial property are set to rise this year by 20 pct to a record level of six billion guilders. (p1)
- Swiss Bank Corporation snatches U.S. investment bank Dillon Read from financial services group ING. (p1)
- Two coalition parties Liberal VVD and D 66 warn that next cabinet will have to make further spending cuts. (p1)
- Foods producer CSM's first half year net rises 8.1 pct to Dfl 101.1 million. (p3)
- Germany's shipyard Meyer is to set up a shipyard in the Eemshaven alone and not together with five Groningen-based shipyards. (p5)
- Large energy producers cooperating in SEP are losing ground to smaller independent ones. (p3)
- Insurer Aegon raises its 1997 profits forecast due to positive bourse climate and currency effects. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Pension fund ABP seeks to put a limit to options schemes for its management. (p1)
- Average capital of Dutch millionaires in the Netherlands dropped in 1994 due to bad bourse climate. (p2)
- Six Dutch banks and financial services institutes win court case to regain their Internet names. (p2)
- Province of North Holland prepared to allow more passengers than the maximum 44 million set for Schiphol Airport around the year 2003. (p7) DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet reaches agreement on more money for solving problems in the home care sector. (p1)
- White civil servants and administrators should be reschooled in contact with minority groups - recommendation from a congress. (p1)
- Sale of its loss-giving chipcard activities brings Philips Electronics 176 million guilders. (p25)
- Shipping company Van Ommeren is ready for acquisitions. (p27) TROUW
- Dutch association of municipalities VNG says six bn guilders is needed to make the big cities livable for people with good salaries. (p4)
- Amsterdam Exchanges and U.K.-based FTSE are to launch a new Euro-Index: the Eurotop 300 index. (p6) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Number of TV producing companies launch attack on entertainment group Endemol's near-monopoly position. (p1)
- Builder NBM-Amstelland sells its ten Belgian Gamma DIY- shops. (p13)
